---
title: "OncoGFR 1200 — Chemotherapy Dosing by eGFR Equation"
---

## Overview

A sub-analysis of the dose project using the **OncoGFR 1200** cohort, which uniquely
includes a **measured GFR (mGFR, ⁵¹Cr-EDTA plasma clearance)** as the gold standard.

The analysis asks: *if chemotherapy were dosed from each estimated-GFR (eGFR) equation
instead of measured GFR, how often would patients be over- or under-dosed?* Results are
presented as **heatmaps** across equations and drugs, on both **indexed** (mL/min/1.73 m²)
and **non-indexed** (absolute mL/min) GFR scales.

- [**Dosing Heatmaps →**](qmd/dosing_heatmap.qmd)
- [**Grant figures →**](qmd/grant.qmd) — carboplatin overdose risk vs the
  eGFR~cr-cys~ / Cockcroft-Gault discordance index

### eGFR equations compared (reference = measured GFR)

Cockcroft-Gault · CKD-EPI Cr (2021) · CKD-EPI Cys · CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (2021) ·
EKFC Cr · EKFC Cys · EKFC Cr-Cys · CKD-EPI 4-marker

### Drugs

Carboplatin (Calvert, ±15 % and ±20 % margins) · Cisplatin · Methotrexate · Melphalan

### B. Derived variables

#### B1 — The analysis variables

| Variable | Type | Definition | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `egfr_pctdiff_cg` | numeric, % | `(CKDEPIcrcys21non_index − CGnon_index) / CGnon_index × 100` | The x-axis of every figure — the Jiaxuan discordance index (**C4**). Both terms absolute mL/min, as specified. |
| `reg` | table, 8 rows | equation id → family, display label, indexed column, absolute column | One registry so a figure loops over equations instead of hard-coding 8 column names. |
| `MGFR` | named vector | `index → mGFRindex`, `nonindex → mGFRnon_index` | Picks the reference column that matches the scale being analysed. Guards against comparing an indexed eGFR to an absolute mGFR. |
| `cls` | Overdose / Underdose / Concordant | `carbo_class()` output per patient × equation | The outcome. Everything plotted is the share of patients with `cls == "Overdose"`. |
| `carbo_nonindex`, `carbo_index` | long tables, 9,600 rows | 1,200 patients × 8 equations, carrying `cls` and `egfr_pctdiff_cg` | Long format lets one plotting function serve all 8 panels. |
| `fried_grp` | factor **NEW** | `fried_classification` 0/1/2 → Non-frail / Pre-frail / Frail | Figure 4. **Mapping is inferred** — the file ships no codebook; the 165/314/113 split matches the standard Fried ordering. Confirm before publishing. |
| `cachexia_grp` | factor **NEW** | `Cachexia` 0/1 → No cachexia / Cachexia | Figure 4. |
| `asgppp_grp` | factor **NEW** | `ASG-PPP` 1/2 → ASG-PPP 1 / ASG-PPP 2 | Figure 4. Left unlabelled — which rating is the worse nutritional state is not documented in the source. |
| `d_hist`, `n_tot`, `q` | data / 1,200 / quartiles | non-missing rows of the index, its N, and its 25/50/75th centiles | Figure 2 and its summary table. |

#### B2 — Classification functions

| Function | Signature | Logic |
|---|---|---|
| `carbo_class()` | `(gfr, mgfr, k_hi = 6, k_lo = 4)` | Overdose if `5(gfr+25) > k_hi·(mgfr+25)`; Underdose if `< k_lo·(mgfr+25)`; else Concordant. Defaults are the ±20 % band (**C3**). |
| `carbo_over_thr()` | `(gfr, mgfr, thr)` **NEW** | Overdose-only indicator at an arbitrary tolerance: `5(gfr+25) > 5(1+thr)(mgfr+25)`. Generalises `carbo_class` so one call covers 10 %, 15 % and 20 %. |
| `build_carbo_long()` | `(scale)` | Expands the wide file to one row per patient × equation on the chosen scale, attaching `cls` and the index. |
| `grant_loess()` | `(cl, eq, direction)` | Fits the smooth, clips it to [0, 100] (**C6**), draws one panel. |

#### B3 — Figure-control constants

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PCTD_CG_XLIM` | `c(-50, 40)` | Plot window for Figures 1 and 3. Holds 98.2 % of patients; keeps the smooth off sparse tails. |
| `PCTD_CG_BREAKS` | `seq(-60, 60, 10)` **NEW** | Ticks every 10 percentage points. Spans the full data range (−52 to +53) so the unclipped distribution is ticked end to end; clipped figures simply drop the breaks outside their window. |
| `REF_LINE` | `-10` **NEW** | The single black dashed reference line, replacing the former grey zero line and solid median line. |
| `pctd_x()` | layer list **NEW** | Shared x-scale + visible black tick marks, so all four figures line up. |
| `ref_vline()` | layer **NEW** | The −10 % dashed rule, defined once. |
| `BINW` | `5` | Histogram bin width, percentage points. |
| `CNT_MAX` | `ceiling(max(count)/25)·25` **NEW** | Tallest bin rounded up to a clean 25. Sets the right-hand axis of the overlay (**C7**). |
| `THRESHOLDS` | `c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20)` **NEW** | The three overdose tolerances in Figure 4. |
| `CARBO_RED` | `#F8766D` | The carboplatin hue from the original 5-drug panels, kept so the line is recognisable. |

#### B4 — Figure 4 summary table

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `domain` **NEW** | Which assessment the grouping comes from: Whole cohort / Fried frailty / Cachexia / ASG-PPP. |
| `grp`, `grp_i` **NEW** | Group label, and its integer level. `grp_i` exists only to preserve clinical ordering — binding rows across domains collapses factors to character, which would sort "Frail, Non-frail, Pre-frail" alphabetically. |
| `N`, `k` **NEW** | Patients in the cell, and how many were overdosed. |

### C. Concepts

**C1 · Measured GFR is the gold standard.** Every "overdose" on this page is defined against
⁵¹Cr-EDTA plasma clearance, not against another estimate. So the figures measure *estimation
error with a clinical consequence*, not disagreement between two guesses.

**C2 · Indexed vs absolute GFR.** Indexed GFR (mL/min/1.73 m²) rescales everyone to a standard
body size — right for *staging* CKD, because it makes patients comparable. Absolute GFR
(mL/min) is the patient's actual clearance — right for *dosing*, because a drug is cleared by
the kidney the patient actually has. The relationship is `absolute = indexed × BSA / 1.73`
(verified in this dataset). Using an indexed GFR in Calvert systematically misdoses anyone
whose body size is far from average, which is why the absolute scale is the primary analysis
here.

**C3 · Calvert and where the constants come from.** Carboplatin is dosed to a target exposure:
`dose = AUC × (GFR + 25)`. At AUC 5 the dose is `5(GFR + 25)`. Overdosing by more than a
fraction *t* means

$$5(\text{eGFR}+25) > (1+t)\cdot 5(\text{mGFR}+25)$$

so the right-hand constant is `5(1+t)`: **5.5** at 10 %, **5.75** at 15 %, **6** at 20 %. The
mirror-image constants `5(1−t)` give underdose. That is the whole of `carbo_class()` and
`carbo_over_thr()` — the apparently magic 6 and 4 are just ±20 %.

**C4 · The discordance index.** `(eGFRcr-cys − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault × 100`.
Cystatin C is not raised by muscle mass, so in a wasted patient creatinine stays deceptively
low and Cockcroft-Gault reads high, while cystatin pulls the combined equation down. A
**negative** index therefore flags "Cockcroft-Gault is flattering this kidney". Because it is
a ratio of two GFRs on the same scale, the BSA factor cancels — indexed and absolute versions
agree to within 0.5 points here (rounding only).

**C5 · Why the index is more discriminating for some equations.** Cockcroft-Gault is the
index's own denominator, so the CG panel is partly self-referential and shows the steepest
gradient (78.5 % → 1.2 %). The CKD-EPI Cr 2021 panel is a genuinely independent test and is
much flatter (33 % → 15 %). Both are shown; only the second is independent evidence.

**C6 · LOESS and the clipping.** The outcome is binary per patient (overdosed or not). LOESS
takes a locally weighted average of those 0/1 values in a sliding window (`span = 0.9`), which
estimates the *probability* of overdose as a smooth function of the index. It is unconstrained,
so where data are sparse it can return values above 100 % or below 0 % — the raw
Cockcroft-Gault fit reached ~105 %. The drawn curve and band are therefore clipped to [0, 100].
The fit is not modified, so a curve lying flat on 0 % at the far right is at the edge of the
data, not a genuine plateau.

**C7 · The dual axis in Figure 3.** Two quantities with different units share one panel. The
overdose curve owns the left axis (0–100 %). The bars are drawn as `count / CNT_MAX × 100` so
they occupy the same 0–100 range, and the right axis inverts exactly that transform to relabel
them as counts (or as % of cohort). Bar *heights are identical* in both variants — only the
right-hand labelling changes. The right axis and the bars share a colour so the mapping needs
no legend.

**C8 · Exact binomial CIs.** Figure 4's smallest cell is 113 patients (Frail) with ~10 events.
Normal-approximation intervals are unreliable that sparse and can run below zero, so the
Clopper-Pearson exact interval is used instead. Overlapping intervals across groups are the
reason the frailty and cachexia contrasts are reported as null.

**C9 · Why the −10 % line.** A single fixed reference at −10 % replaces the old zero line and
cohort-median line. Zero is not the clinically interesting point — it is where two *estimates*
agree, which says nothing about dosing. −10 % sits where the overdose curve begins to climb
steeply, so it reads as a candidate flag threshold rather than a statistical artefact.
